summary:
Aysén del General Carlos Ibáñez del Campo stands under Chile's national framework; the national record carries the gender recognition, marriage, anti-discrimination and migration provisions that apply in the region. The Outright International Chile country dossier, published 12 March 2026, carries no Aysén-specific legal, incident or enforcement finding.

Movilh's XXIV annual report (HECHOS 2025, published March 2026) places Aysén at 0.65% of nationally documented cases of discrimination and abuse, a rise of 25% year on year. The report warns that a share this low reflects weaker local safety rather than low risk to LGBT people in the region.
tangentialFactors: Movilh reads Aysén's rise as part of a wider shift in which documented cases increased across most of Chile's regions while falling in only two, and attributes that pattern to hatred expanding into regions with less public debate. The regional breakdown is a share of the national total, so Aysén's 0.65% is a proportion of all documented cases rather than a count of local incidents.
localsOnly: No Aysén-specific resident-facing finding was identified. The sources record no local service, local enforcement practice or local protection machinery operating in the region.
outOfScopeNotes: The 2024 Aysén share is not reproduced in the 2025 Movilh edition, so the year-on-year change cannot be checked against the earlier figure. The exclusion of the Gender Identity Support Program from the 2026 budget bill is a national measure carried by the national record, not a region-specific finding.
